translation:
Zulana

When Radhavdas Maharaj had gone on pilgrimage, he made a night halt near Zulana. Then, at night, robbers attempted to loot the group (sangh), but seeing the Lord protecting them, they were not able to carry out the robbery. Having heard the praise of the protecting Lord, the Thakor of that place, Gumansinh, made Radhavdasji his guru. Thus, after Naranadas of Bareli, Gumansinh of Zulana became an udabhakt (awakened devotee). In Vikram Samvat 2024, when [the author] went to Zulana, the Thakor of that place, Vishveshwarsharansinh Das, met me. He was 60 years old. From him I obtained four handwritten manuscripts (granths). In one of those manuscripts the kirtans of Adhyaru were written; it is written therein that it was written for the reading of the young Thakor Gumansinhji of Zulana. Furthermore, a manuscript of Gumansinh was also obtained from Kuvarpura. Thus this Zulana too is a punya sthan (sacred place) of another devotee of Malva.
